text: No, I haven't had any fever, night sweats, or lost any weight. I do have a history of smoking, about a pack a day for twenty years, but I don't think I've been around anyone with tuberculosis.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your significant smoking history and the duration of symptoms, I need to rule out lung cancer or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray. Do you experience wheezing or shortness of breath specifically when you exercise?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Hyperinflated lungs, flattened diaphragms, no acute infiltrates or obvious masses.

speaker: Doctor
text: The X-ray findings of hyperinflated lungs and flattened diaphragms are classic signs of COPD. Do you experience significant shortness of breath even during mild activities like walking or climbing stairs? Additionally, do you notice any swelling in your ankles or legs?

speaker: Patient
text: Yes, I get quite winded even when I'm just walking to the mailbox or climbing a single flight of stairs. As for my legs, I haven't noticed any swelling, though I do feel generally short of breath during my usual weekend basketball games.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD), likely emphysema predominant.
